newsitem.title: CHINA: Government House starts new life in stormy HK.
newsitem.headline: Government House starts new life in stormy HK.

text.p: Government House, long a symbol of British colonial rule, started a new life under the red flag of China on Wednesday with Chief Executive Tung Chee-hwa using the venue to entertain visiting ministers and hand out medals.
As lightning flashed and torrential rain pounded Hong Kong, a string of limousines purred up the drive of the neo-classical mansion perched on the slopes of Hong Kong island.
Tung has said he would not live in Government House, home to generations of British governors, but would use the stately home as a meeting place and turn part of it into a museum.
Just two days after he was sworn in on July 1 and Hong Kong reverted to Chinese rule, Government House was again the centre of attention.
Tung first met a succession of politicians from New Zealand, Canada, Japan and Thailand, then presided over the awarding of Grand Bauhinia medals -- Hong Kong's new post-colonial honours.
Britain held its own final honours ceremony on Sunday, conducted by heir to the throne Prince Charles and the 28th and last governor, Chris Patten.

Patten vacated the building on Monday, and the Union flag was furled and royal insignia and portraits were removed from the building, to be replaced by the flags and insignia of China and its new Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.
Tung ruled out living in the house because of its bad fung shui, an age-old Chinese belief that harmony with the elements ensures good fortune.
"I have heard the Government House is crowded and the fung shui is not good," Tung told a China-controlled selection committee last year.

But his decision may have also been motivated by a desire to distance himself from any colonial baggage, such as living in a mansion, which has been a home from home for 25 of the last 28 governors sent out from Britain.
Surrounded by skyscrapers, Government House has commanding views over some of the most expensive real estate in the world.
